summary.name: 3D Diorama, category Digital and 3D Aesthetics. The label was normalized, and the source explicitly names a 3D diorama. Treat it as a miniature-stage style.
summary.visualIdentity: Explicit: a bounded miniature stage with consistent scale for architecture, characters and props, seen from an elevated or oblique camera. Limited depth of field must not blur key models or paths. Local actions and environmental detail stay readable.
summary.suitableUses: Inferred from the listed best-for examples: miniature sets as the subject, story-driven miniature worlds, seasonal campaigns, explainers with characters, campus maps, product ecosystems and process tours. The source names no other audiences or industries, so those remain unspecified.
summary.limitations: Explicit: avoid mixing glossy and matte character finishes, oversized figures, stop-motion labeling, notes covering key models, and annotations during camera moves. Renders are simulated appearance, not photographed production. Soft shadows alone do not establish photorealism.
summary.palette: Reference-dependent optional example, not an intrinsic style palette: background #EEE6D4, foreground #35433C, accent_1 #7B9173, accent_2 #B3885F, with no gradient. Task-supplied exact colors override these values. Only foreground on background (8.371:1) passes body-text contrast; the accent pairs (3.04 and 3.27) are decorative only. Checks are two-color only and must be rechecked on composited frames.
summary.motionAndInteraction: Explicit: smooth authored movement with deliberate cuts, impacts and reading holds, with one owner per animated property. Reference patterns include bounded depth parallax, a full camera orbit that needs complete geometry, chapter handoffs, storytelling, exploded reveals of separable parts only, a real-depth dolly and a camera orbit. Video uses composition time; pointer and scroll input belongs only to interactive delivery.
summary.audio: Unspecified for this style: no genre, tempo, instrument, voice or mandatory layer is fixed. Propose audio from the topic, audience and storyboard, and honor explicit user audio choices first. Inferred: restrained ambience or sparse accents may suit a miniature world, but this is unconfirmed. Keep speech clear and never invent available audio assets.
summary.assetRequirements: Explicit needs: authorized 3D models and materials at consistent scale, normal and roughness maps treated as non-color data, and authorized footage for any video screens. Orbits need complete geometry or sufficient turntable views, creature assets are needed only for the optional hop, and fonts must be local. Filenames and exporter strings do not establish authorship, license or animation clips.
summary.combinations: Use the diorama alone when the miniature set is the subject. Hybrid with style-078 for matte clay-like figures that share the light rig and fixed scale, or with style-024 for hand-drawn callouts in foreground ink with at most one accent. Palette comes from the reference scene, and new accent hues are to be avoided.
summary.productionApproach: Style renderer: Blender with Python bpy and Cycles or EEVEE, plus optional toon-ramp, outline, soft-lighting and CRT techniques. Motion engine: Blender keyframes, glTF part animation, and raycasting for interactive use only. Pipeline: HyperFrames handles composition and export with a GSAP paused timeline; Remotion is used only for a recorded fallback reason. Verify key frames, seeks, audio sync and loop seams.
